title: Customer Support Chatbot
description: A public chatbot that answers customer questions using product docs and account history.
business_goal: Resolve common support tickets automatically and cut call center volume.
users: All customers of the platform (public interface), plus support agents.

architecture.name: Customers
architecture.purpose: Anyone with a web browser can chat with the assistant from the public site.
security_considerations: Unauthenticated users form the primary threat surface
architecture.attack_surface: An anonymous user is one crafted prompt away from abusing the system.

architecture.name: Support Portal
architecture.purpose: Chat widget embedded in the customer portal with a login for account-linked answers.
security_considerations: Authentication is optional for most questions
architecture.attack_surface: An attacker logs in as a victim and asks account questions.

architecture.name: AI Gateway
architecture.purpose: Routes chatbot requests, applies prompt filters, and enforces answer policy.
security_considerations: Filtering is the main defense and is lightly configured
architecture.attack_surface: Malicious prompts pass through because filtering is weak.

architecture.name: LLM
architecture.purpose: Generates conversational answers to customer questions.
security_considerations: Hosted model processes all public prompts
Answers must be grounded in product docs
architecture.attack_surface: Jailbreaks and injections turn the model into a tool for the attacker.

architecture.name: Knowledge Base
architecture.purpose: Embeds product documentation and curated FAQ content.
security_considerations: Should contain only approved public docs
Account data must not be indexed here
architecture.attack_surface: If internal docs are indexed, the chatbot leaks them.

architecture.name: Account Data
architecture.purpose: Customer order history and account details used for account-linked answers.
security_considerations: Only the logged-in customer's own data should be available
architecture.attack_surface: The model retrieves another customer's order details.

architecture.name: Chat Logging
architecture.purpose: Stores transcripts for QA and dispute resolution.
architecture.attack_surface: Long-lived transcripts become a data breach waiting to happen.

architecture.name: Answer Monitoring
architecture.purpose: Tracks satisfaction and flagged bad answers.
architecture.attack_surface: Abusive or dangerous answers are not caught until a customer reports them.

threats.name: Public jailbreak attempts
threats.description: Anonymous users use roleplay and framing tricks to bypass the assistant's rules.
threats.business_consequences: The chatbot gives harmful or off-policy answers at scale.

threats.name: Injection through support text
threats.description: A user pastes injection text that the chatbot follows instead of its instructions.
threats.business_consequences: The assistant is hijacked to do things it was not built to do.

threats.name: Cross-customer data leak
threats.description: The model retrieves or repeats another customer's order details.
threats.business_consequences: A privacy breach affecting many customers and trust in the brand.

threats.name: Transcripts held too long
threats.description: Chat logs with personal data are stored without a retention limit.
threats.business_consequences: Every transcript is a potential future breach.

threats.name: Prompt cost abuse
threats.description: Automated traffic pumps prompts to exhaust the budget or trigger rate limits.
threats.business_consequences: Rising cost and degraded service for real customers.

threats.name: Account-linked answers without checks
threats.description: The assistant answers account questions without verifying the session belongs to the account.
threats.business_consequences: Customer account details are disclosed to the wrong person.

threats.name: Invented policies
threats.description: The model invents refund or shipping policies that the company never offered.
threats.business_consequences: Customers act on wrong information and disputes increase.

teaching_points: A public chatbot is the highest-exposure AI you can build because anyone can reach it.
Jailbreaks and injections are the default threat for anonymous users.
Retrieval must be scoped to the logged-in user, never the whole database.
Rate limits protect budget and service availability, not only security.
